_note: Sources for Form 2 History (Batches Y2-1 and Y2-2, Terms 1 and 2). All answers are authored facts: a History teacher must check them.

early-peoples.ref: The peopling of Cameroon: the Pygmies (Baka, Bagyeli/Bakola, Bedzan) and the Sao civilisation south of Lake Chad (Cameroonian History textbooks; archaeological work in the Lake Chad basin)
early-peoples.supports: Location and way of life of the Pygmies; the Sao's walled towns, pottery, bronze work and burial jars; their decline under Kanem-Bornu (about 15th–16th centuries); the Kotoko as partly descended from them.
early-peoples.checked: General knowledge, not opened in this session; dates are approximate and given as such. Please check.

migrations.ref: Migration waves into Cameroon (Bantu, semi-Bantu/Grassfields, Sudanese, Fulani, Shuwa Arabs, Hausa); the Fulani jihad of Modibo Adama (from 1809) and the Adamawa emirate
migrations.supports: Groupings of peoples and their regions; causes and effects of migration; “Africa in miniature”; over 250 ethnic groups.
migrations.checked: Standard textbook groupings; the classification of individual peoples should be checked by the teacher.

precolonial-societies.ref: Centralised (state-like) and egalitarian (segmentary) societies of pre-colonial Cameroon
precolonial-societies.supports: Lamidates (lamido), Bamum (sultan; Njoya, about 1886–1933, Bamum script; capital Foumban), Grassfields chiefdoms (fon), Mandara; Beti, Bassa, Bakweri, Mafa as egalitarian societies.
precolonial-societies.checked: General knowledge: please check the examples and Njoya's dates. The sheet's “Equalisation states” is read as egalitarian societies.

ancient-ghana.ref: Ancient Ghana (Wagadu) of the Soninke; Koumbi Saleh; the trans-Saharan gold and salt trade; the Almoravids (1076)
ancient-ghana.supports: Location (today's Mauritania and Mali), titles of the king, the twin-town capital, the trade, taxes and decline.
ancient-ghana.checked: Standard textbook account; the 1076 date is debated by historians but standard in schools. Please check.

historical-enquiry.ref: Methods of historical enquiry: oral traditions, archaeology, languages, written accounts; interviewing respectfully
historical-enquiry.supports: The steps of the two guided works and the further study.

african-states.ref: Mali, Kanem-Bornu, Kongo and Great Zimbabwe (9th–16th centuries); factors in the decline of African empires
african-states.supports: Kirina 1235, Mansa Musa (about 1312–1337, pilgrimage 1324), Timbuktu, Songhai (Sonni Ali takes Timbuktu 1468; Tondibi 1591); Saifawa Mai, Njimi, the Bulala, Ngazargamu, Idris Alooma (about 1571–1603); Lukeni lua Nimi, Manikongo, Mbanza Kongo, Diogo Cão 1483, João I 1491, Afonso I 1506–1543, Mbwila 1665; Great Zimbabwe about 1300–1450, dry-stone walls, soapstone birds, Mutapa; Almoravids 1076. Years between events are computed by subtraction.
african-states.checked: Dates from general knowledge, not opened in this session (several are approximate and vary between textbooks): please check them.

african-arts.ref: African arts: Nok, Igbo-Ukwu, Ife, Benin; Cameroonian arts (Bamum, Bamileke, Foumban casting, Tikar); the lost-wax method; functions of art
african-arts.supports: Examples, the lost-wax steps and the functions (religious, political, social, economic, decorative).
african-arts.checked: General knowledge: please check the dates of Nok, Igbo-Ukwu and Ife.

external-contacts.ref: The trans-Saharan trade; the Portuguese on the West African coast (Henry the Navigator, Elmina 1482); the Indian Ocean trade (monsoons, dhows, Swahili city-states, Zheng He, Vasco da Gama at Malindi 1498); the first contact of Cameroon with Europeans (Fernando Pó about 1472, Rio dos Camarões, the Duala middlemen)
external-contacts.supports: Goods traded, results of the contacts, the origin of the name Cameroon, the Baptist mission 1841–1845.
external-contacts.checked: General knowledge: please check the dates and the monsoon months.

medieval-europe.ref: Europe from the Dark Ages to the Renaissance: fall of Rome 476, Charlemagne 800, feudalism, the Crusades 1096–1291, the Black Death 1347–1351, the Renaissance in Italy, Gutenberg about 1450
medieval-europe.supports: The feudal roles, the main events and the meaning of the Renaissance.
